chapters.screenText: Ask: how does +15 m thickness change this native shelf result?
chapters.screenWhy: Answer a controlled question with fixed scripts, mesh and runtime controls.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep scripts and controls fixed; change the full synthetic thickness input.
chapters.title: Goal and prerequisites
instructions: First complete the baseline HDF5 guide and retain its result archive.
Open CryoLauncher with a verified BYO AWS connection. Download run.py, initial_fields.py and icepack-shelf-initial-plus15m.h5.
chapters.note: This synthetic sensitivity case changes interior and inflow thickness together. Base and surface are adjusted consistently with flotation; initial velocity stays fixed.
chapters.why: Answer a controlled question with fixed scripts, mesh and runtime controls.

chapters.screenText: Name a separate workspace example. Choose New example.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep baseline and variant examples separate for comparison.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: a new owned Icepack example.
chapters.title: 1. Create a separate example
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack. In Editor enter pilot-icepack-problem-1119 or another unique name.
Choose New example. Keep the accepted baseline example and results for comparison.
chapters.why: Keep baseline and variant examples separate for comparison.

chapters.screenText: Choose the two scripts: run.py and initial_fields.py.
chapters.screenWhy: Both files validate and initialize the native model fields.
chapters.expectedResult: Check Choose script files (2) before importing.
chapters.title: 2. Select both scripts
instructions: Choose Choose script files. Select run.py and initial_fields.py, then Open.
Check that two files are selected.
chapters.why: Both files validate and initialize the native model fields.

chapters.screenText: Enable Replace existing script files, then Import script files.
chapters.screenWhy: Replace prevents a starter or older entrypoint from taking precedence.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: both filenames imported and saved.
chapters.title: 3. Import and save the scripts
instructions: Enable Replace existing script files so an existing starter entrypoint cannot take precedence.
Choose Import script files; wait for the saved confirmation.
chapters.why: Replace prevents a starter or older entrypoint from taking precedence.

chapters.screenText: Read the saved confirmation for both filenames.
chapters.screenWhy: The saved source bytes are what the next run stages.
chapters.expectedResult: Set Run target to run.py.
chapters.title: 4. Confirm the saved entrypoint
instructions: Check Imported run.py, initial_fields.py. Files are saved.
Select run.py as Run target in Experiment before launching.
chapters.note: The two script hashes are unchanged from the accepted baseline HDF5 case.
chapters.why: The saved source bytes are what the next run stages.

chapters.screenText: In Datasets choose icepack-shelf-initial-plus15m.h5.
chapters.screenWhy: Select the full +15 m field dataset rather than editing one mesh node.
chapters.expectedResult: Check that one data file is selected.
chapters.title: 5. Choose the variant dataset
instructions: Scroll to Datasets. Choose Choose data files.
Select icepack-shelf-initial-plus15m.h5 and choose Open. Check the count is one.
chapters.note: The supplied file is a 5 × 9 synthetic structured HDF5 grid, not a Firedrake checkpoint.
chapters.why: Select the full +15 m field dataset rather than editing one mesh node.

chapters.screenText: Choose Upload to store the selected variant.
chapters.screenWhy: Uploading stores the variant in your workspace dataset library.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: Uploaded: icepack-shelf-initial-plus15m.h5.
chapters.title: 6. Upload the selected variant
instructions: Choose Upload to store the selected variant.
Wait for the uploaded filename and select that variant in the dataset list.
chapters.why: Uploading stores the variant in your workspace dataset library.

chapters.screenText: Select the uploaded +15 m variant.
chapters.screenWhy: Choosing the variant keeps the accepted baseline input unchanged.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep the baseline file separate.
chapters.title: 7. Select the variant
instructions: Check the uploaded filename and highlight icepack-shelf-initial-plus15m.h5.
chapters.note: The baseline and variant have different hashes. Their x/y grids, initial vx/vy and floating mask are identical.
chapters.why: Choosing the variant keeps the accepted baseline input unchanged.

chapters.screenText: Enter the alias icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.screenWhy: An alias lets unchanged run.py read the new dataset at its fixed path.
chapters.expectedResult: The fixed script reads data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.title: 8. Set the staged alias
instructions: In the path/alias field enter icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
Do not change the script path: run.py reads data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.note: The filename of the uploaded variant is different from its staged alias.
chapters.why: An alias lets unchanged run.py read the new dataset at its fixed path.

chapters.screenText: Choose Reference in example to attach the variant.
chapters.screenWhy: The attachment binds this variant to the current owned example.
chapters.expectedResult: Bind the selected variant to this owned example.
chapters.title: 9. Attach the variant
instructions: Choose Reference in example with the variant selected and the alias entered.
The reference is copied to the script path when the next run is staged.
chapters.why: The attachment binds this variant to the current owned example.

chapters.screenText: Read the reference confirmation and exact script path.
chapters.screenWhy: The exact path proves what will be copied at the next staging step.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: variant → data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.title: 10. Verify the binding
instructions: Read Referenced icepack-shelf-initial-plus15m.h5. In your script, read data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
Check that this dataset is referenced by the current example.
chapters.note: Accepted staged inputs later matched both script hashes and the variant dataset hash exactly.
chapters.why: The exact path proves what will be copied at the next staging step.

chapters.screenText: Open Review & Launch.
chapters.screenWhy: The review is the final check before an explicit paid submission.
chapters.expectedResult: Review this Icepack example and your resource settings.
chapters.title: 11. Review the native plan
instructions: Check Icepack, the new owned example and run.py. Open Review & Launch.
Confirm the verified BYO connection, qualified image, resource and time-limit settings.
chapters.note: The accepted run retained the baseline scripts, image, 2 vCPU, 8 GiB and 3600-second task timeout.
chapters.why: The review is the final check before an explicit paid submission.

chapters.screenText: Confirm Icepack and the new Own Problem example.
chapters.screenWhy: This prevents a previous example from being mistaken for the new plan.
chapters.expectedResult: The review is bound to this example before explicit submission.
chapters.title: 11. Confirm the reviewed example
instructions: Confirm Model ICEPACK and Example pilot-icepack-problem-1119 in the expanded review.
Keep the qualified image and baseline resource controls unchanged.
chapters.why: This prevents a previous example from being mistaken for the new plan.

chapters.screenText: Scroll through the review. All infrastructure rows must be Ready.
chapters.screenWhy: Ready checks confirm storage, image and compute can support the run.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep the explicit launch action separate from review.
chapters.title: 12. Check readiness
instructions: In the expanded review scroll to Infrastructure.
Check that account, storage, image and compute are ready.
chapters.why: Ready checks confirm storage, image and compute can support the run.

chapters.screenText: Choose Launch cloud run.
chapters.screenWhy: This action stages the bound data and starts one native execution.
chapters.expectedResult: The reviewed variant is staged for one native execution.
chapters.title: 13. Launch explicitly
instructions: Scroll to the bottom of the review and read the final notice.
Choose Launch cloud run. Stay on the page while the selected input is staged.
chapters.why: This action stages the bound data and starts one native execution.

chapters.screenText: Follow the new Icepack run until Completed.
chapters.screenWhy: The new run is the record to follow through startup and completion.
chapters.expectedResult: Startup and Batch task time are recorded separately.
chapters.title: 14. Monitor the selected run
instructions: Confirm that the new Cloud run names the owned Own Problem example.
Wait for Completed, then open View results.
chapters.note: Recorded startup 226.749 s; Batch task 47.298 s; submission-to-stop 274.047 s. The tutorial skips waiting time.
chapters.why: The new run is the record to follow through startup and completion.

chapters.screenText: In Results choose thickness.
chapters.screenWhy: Selecting a field does not itself update the displayed plot.
chapters.expectedResult: Choose the field before rendering it.
chapters.title: 15. Select thickness
instructions: Open Results for the completed variant run.
Select the thickness field. The plot is updated only after Render.
chapters.why: Selecting a field does not itself update the displayed plot.

chapters.screenText: Choose Render for thickness.
chapters.screenWhy: Render displays the final thickness exported by the native solver.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: 25 native values, about 315–515 m.
chapters.title: 16. Render native thickness
instructions: Choose Render.
Read the new thickness summary and colorbar.
chapters.why: Render displays the final thickness exported by the native solver.

chapters.screenText: Select velocity to inspect the native flow field.
chapters.screenWhy: Use velocity to inspect the response to the thickness change.
chapters.expectedResult: The plot changes only after Render.
chapters.title: 17. Select native velocity
instructions: Select velocity in the Field dropdown.
Choose Render next to update the plot.
chapters.why: Use velocity to inspect the response to the thickness change.

chapters.screenText: Choose Render for the selected velocity field.
chapters.screenWhy: Render updates the plot to the selected native velocity field.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: native speed 100–158.61 m/year.
chapters.title: 17. Render native velocity
instructions: With velocity selected, choose Render.
Read the speed summary with its m/year units.
chapters.why: Render updates the plot to the selected native velocity field.

chapters.screenText: Choose Download results. Wait for a fresh archive link.
chapters.screenWhy: Preserve the fields and initialization evidence with runtime metadata.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep the mesh, fields and provenance together.
chapters.title: 18. Prepare the archive
instructions: Scroll below the field and choose Download results.
Wait for a fresh results_bundle link for the selected variant run.
chapters.why: Preserve the fields and initialization evidence with runtime metadata.

chapters.screenText: Choose the fresh results_bundle link to save it.
chapters.screenWhy: Both archives are needed for the baseline-versus-variant comparison.
chapters.expectedResult: Retain both baseline and variant archives.
chapters.title: 19. Save both records
instructions: Choose the newly prepared archive link.
Save the variant beside the accepted baseline archive and keep their hashes in the comparison record.
chapters.why: Both archives are needed for the baseline-versus-variant comparison.

chapters.screenText: Inspect initial-conditions.png from the saved run.
chapters.screenWhy: Check that the uploaded full fields actually initialized the native mesh.
chapters.expectedResult: All five initial fields matched interpolation at all 25 native vertices.
chapters.title: 20. Verify what initialized the model
instructions: Open initial-conditions.png and initial-fields-on-native-mesh.npz from the saved archive.
Thickness, base, surface, vx and vy matched independent interpolation at all native scalar/vector nodes.
chapters.note: All 45 source-grid thickness values are +15 m; flotation-consistent base/surface adjustment is retained, with unchanged initial velocity.
chapters.why: Check that the uploaded full fields actually initialized the native mesh.

chapters.screenText: Derived from saved numeric fields: compare final thickness.
chapters.screenWhy: Shared scales show the two fields; the separate delta scale shows their difference.
chapters.expectedResult: Area-mean thickness: 403.64986 → 418.64758 m.
chapters.title: 21. Compare thickness
instructions: Read the baseline and variant on the shared thickness scale. Read the difference on its separate scale.
The final area-mean thickness increased by 14.99772 m after one 0.01-year step.
chapters.note: Derived scientific plot from verified numeric output archives, not GUI footage. The complete figure and per-node deltas are available with this chapter.
chapters.why: Shared scales show the two fields; the separate delta scale shows their difference.

chapters.screenText: Derived from saved numeric fields: compare final speed.
chapters.screenWhy: Area-weighted metrics compare the full field rather than one selected node.
chapters.expectedResult: Area-RMS speed: 133.90846 → 137.17064 m/year.
chapters.title: 22. Compare speed
instructions: Read baseline and variant speed on the same scale; use the separate scale for the difference.
The area-RMS speed increased by 3.26217 m/year in this recorded pair.
chapters.note: Derived scientific plot from the two verified archives. The mesh remained 25 vertices and 32 triangles over 100 km².
chapters.why: Area-weighted metrics compare the full field rather than one selected node.

chapters.screenText: Keep the input change and controls with your comparison.
chapters.screenWhy: Retain the coupled input change so the scientific question stays clear.
chapters.expectedResult: This pair changes interior and inflow thickness together.
chapters.title: 23. Interpret and retain the evidence
instructions: Keep the two unchanged scripts, dataset hashes, mesh, runtime versions and controls with both result archives.
The perturbation changes thickness inside the shelf and the script’s thickness_inflow condition together.
chapters.note: This one synthetic sensitivity pair is not an independent baseline repeat or an accuracy result.
chapters.why: Retain the coupled input change so the scientific question stays clear.
